purpose: This tool shows why we invent the number i and where complex numbers live. You see that a number a + bi is just a point, and you add, measure and mirror numbers by moving points on a plane.

stops.title: The figure changes by step
stops.text: Step 1 is the curve y = x^2 + 1 with a point you can drag. Later steps show the powers of i on a wheel, then the complex plane with real part across and imaginary part up. Points z and w are blue and red, and you drag them.
stops.try: Answer the prediction. Then drag the point along the curve and watch its height.

stops.title: Move the point
stops.text: Slides the point along the curve y = x^2 + 1. Its height never gets to 0, so no real x can solve x^2 = -1. This is why we invent i. It stays locked until you predict.
stops.try: Slide x from -3 to 3. What is the lowest height?

stops.title: Next changes the scene
stops.text: There is no menu here, so Next and Back switch the tool. Step 2 simplifies roots of negative numbers, step 3 steps round the wheel of powers of i, step 4 gives four plane tools: plot, add and subtract, size, mirror.

stops.title: Try practice problems
stops.text: Eight short problems. Press the same button to go back to the lesson. Nothing is saved or scored.

stops.title: Quick check
stops.text: A short exit ticket with explained answers.

teacher: Ask for the prediction in step 1 before anyone drags. Ask: why is root of -4 times root of -9 not root of 36? Misconception: treating bi as the imaginary part when it is b. Project step 4 with Add and subtract and drag w.
